diagrams.title: Trust Zones and Zero Trust Path
diagrams.subtitle: From untrusted traffic to the resource: every crossing verifies identity, device, and privilege.

nodes.label: Untrust
nodes.detail: No implicit trust: every inbound flow is suspect, even if it later originates from the internal network.
nodes.exam: Zero Trust makes no trust distinction between 'inside' and 'outside'.

nodes.label: DMZ
nodes.detail: Perimeter firewall, proxy, and detective sensors. Public-facing servers are exposed there without exposing the internal network.
nodes.exam: A detective IDS is placed out-of-band (SPAN/tap); a preventive IPS is inline.

nodes.label: Identity verification
nodes.detail: MFA, federation, and least privilege: the user is authenticated on every session, not once and for all.
nodes.exam: A VPN authenticates the tunnel; Zero Trust authenticates the user and the resource.

nodes.label: Health & inventory
nodes.detail: Patches, antivirus, encryption, and presence in inventory. An unknown device is denied or quarantined.
nodes.exam: Device health and device inventory are two distinct controls in §3.2.

nodes.label: Out-of-band
nodes.detail: Separate management network, single bastion entry point with MFA and session recording.
nodes.exam: Administration never traverses the user network in a mature architecture.

nodes.label: Application access
nodes.detail: Minimal access to the requested resource, continuously reassessed. gMSAs avoid hardcoded service passwords.
nodes.exam: SSE and gMSA are from objective §3.2, absent from the four provided books.

nodes.label: Internal trust
nodes.detail: Internal firewall and segmentation limit lateral movement between departments.
nodes.exam: The failure mode (fail-open / fail-closed) is decided based on service criticality.

quiz.question: Which node verifies that the device is known and healthy before application access?
